summary: Players' inventories, held by the server. Each change is all or nothing, and returns { ok, code, revision, items }. A refused change has ok false and a code, such as invalidItem, invalidAmount, insufficientItems, inventoryCapacity, unknownItem or staleRevision. Passing `revision` refuses the request if the inventory has changed. Rows are { id, item, name, amount, quality, health, condition, equipped, metadata }. Events are playerInventoryReady, playerInventoryChanged and playerItemUsed. Inventory.beforeCommit makes what players' own actions move wait for a resource's verdict. On the client, Inventory.whenUsed takes over chosen items' actions on the inventory screen.

classes.summary: All item classes in the game's catalogue, with id, name, nameKey, category, maximumQuality, quest, slot and model, the ground mesh, or '' if the tables give none.
classes.exampleLua:
local swords = {}
for _, itemClass in ipairs(kcds.players.Inventory.classes()) do
  if string.find(itemClass.name, "Sword", 1, true) then
    table.insert(swords, itemClass)
  end
end

setWearRates.summary: Scales how fast items wear, where 1 is the game's rate, 0 none and 2 twice as fast. A rate for an item, by table name or GUID, beats its category, such as meleeWeapon, missileWeapon, armor, helmet, hood or ammo, which beats `default`. Repairs are never scaled.

itemPrice.summary: The game's price for one unit, in money units, which are tenths of a groschen. `pristine` is at the best health its quality allows, and `current` at its own health. Null for an unknown class.

params.item: The item class, by name or GUID.

itemPrice.exampleLua:
local price = kcds.players.Inventory.itemPrice("apple")
if price then
  print("new " .. tostring(price.pristine) .. ", as it is " .. tostring(price.current))
end

renameItem.summary: Renames an item in all players' games, along with other classes sharing its name, until the server stops. null restores the game's name. Returns the GUIDs renamed.
renameItem.exampleLua:
local Inventory = kcds.players.Inventory

Inventory.renameItem("apple", "Rattay apple")
Inventory.renameItem("apple", null)

overrideStats.summary: Overrides a class's combat values for all current and future players until the server stops, or restores them with null or {}. Values belong to the class, so all copies change and apply from the next hit. A set names only the stats it changes, and replaces the previous set entirely, while Items.override's weight, price, max and durability stay. A melee weapon takes attack, attackModStab, attackModSlash, attackModSmash, defense, strReq and agiReq. Armour, a helmet or a hood takes defenseStab, defenseSlash, defenseSmash, noise and strReq. A missile weapon takes power, defense, strReq and agiReq, while limbResistance is not supported yet and throws. Ammunition takes attackStab, attackSlash, attackSmash and powerMod. Throws a TypeError for an unknown class, a class with none of these, a name its kind lacks, or a value out of range. Returns true.

params.item: The item class, by table name or GUID.
params.stats: The numbers by name, or null for the original values.

overrideStats.exampleLua:
local Inventory = kcds.players.Inventory

Inventory.overrideStats("longSwordDuel", { attack = 210, strReq = 12 })
Inventory.overrideStats("longSwordDuel", null)
overrideStats.exampleCs:
Inventory.OverrideStats("longSwordDuel", new { attack = 210, strReq = 12 });
Inventory.OverrideStats("longSwordDuel", Sdk.Null);

itemStats.summary: The combat numbers overrideStats set on a class, by name, or null if unchanged. The server does not read the game's numbers. Throws a TypeError for an unknown class.

params.item: The item class, by table name or GUID.

get.summary: A player's inventory as { revision, items, quickslots, ready }, or null.
get.exampleLua:
local stock = kcds.players.Inventory.get(player)
local coins = 0
for _, row in ipairs(stock and stock.items or {}) do
  if row.name == "money" then
    coins = coins + row.amount
  end
end

add.summary: Adds units of one item class to the row with the same properties, or a new row.

params.request: { item, amount, metadata?, revision?, notify? }. `metadata` takes quality, health or condition, poison, poisonCharges, onEquipBuffs, and custom { name, description, data }, where data is a plain object up to 16 KiB as JSON, not text. Other values end with invalidMetadata. `transient: true` makes a row that leaves when its player disconnects, before playerDisconnect, so saving the inventory there leaves it out, suiting a sack over the head or a punishment prop. `notify: false` shows no 'You received' notice.

add.exampleLua:
local answer = kcds.players.Inventory.add(player, { item = "apple", amount = 3 })
if not answer.ok then
  print("refused: " .. tostring(answer.code))
end

params.request: { units: [{ id, amount }], revision?, notify? }, with row ids from Inventory.get.

remove.exampleLua:
local Inventory = kcds.players.Inventory

local apples = nil
for _, row in ipairs(Inventory.get(player).items) do
  if row.name == "apple" then
    apples = row
    break
  end
end
if apples then
  Inventory.remove(player, { units = { { id = apples.id, amount = 1 } } })
end

editCustom.summary: Changes only the named custom fields of a row, and null resets one. A row's own name and description show in its player's inventory and item panel for every kind of item (a renamed sword stays a sword for equipping and combat).

params.request: { id, name?, description?, data?, revision? }, where data is a plain object, not text.

editCustom.example: kcds.players.Inventory.editCustom(player, { id: row.id, name: 'Letter to the burgrave' });
editCustom.exampleLua: kcds.players.Inventory.editCustom(player, { id = row.id, name = "Letter to the burgrave" })
editCustom.exampleCs: Inventory.EditCustom(player, new { id = row["id"], name = "Letter to the burgrave" });

editRow.summary: Replaces a row's properties, keeping its id and amount.
editRow.exampleCs: Inventory.EditRow(player, new { id = row["id"], metadata = new { quality = 4 } });

set.summary: Replaces the whole inventory. Equipped pieces must fit on a body together, otherwise it returns invalidEquipment with `conflicts` saying why (as Player.equip).
set.exampleLua: kcds.players.Inventory.set(player, { items = { { item = "money", amount = 100 }, { item = "apple", amount = 3 } } })
set.exampleCs: Inventory.Set(player, new { items = new object[] { new { item = "money", amount = 100 }, new { item = "apple", amount = 3 } } });

transfer.summary: Moves exact units with their properties between inventories, all or nothing.
transfer.exampleLua:
-- The buyer hands over 10 groschen.
local Inventory = kcds.players.Inventory

local purse = nil
for _, row in ipairs(Inventory.get(buyer).items) do
  if row.name == "money" then
    purse = row
    break
  end
end
Inventory.transfer(buyer, seller, { units = { { id = purse.id, amount = 100 } } })

stolenMarks.summary: Whether the game marks items as stolen.

setStolenMarks.summary: Turns the game's stolen marks, the red hand and merchants refusing stolen goods, on or off for all players.

whenUsed.summary: Client only. Takes over an item's actions on the inventory screen: 'secondary' to eat, drink or apply, 'primary' for the hint bar's action, and 'activate' for the equip toggle. The game then does nothing itself, and the handler receives { item, uid, id, revision, amount, action }, so consume anything on the server. The newest handler for an item instance beats one for its class. Returns the registration id.

params.item: An item class, by name or GUID, a type from Items.register, or { uid } of one item.

stopWhenUsed.summary: Client only. Removes a whenUsed handler.
stopWhenUsed.exampleLua:
-- client
local Inventory = kcds.players.Inventory

local handlerId = Inventory.whenUsed("herb_mint", function() end)
Inventory.stopWhenUsed(handlerId)

beforeCommit.summary: Makes what players' own actions do to inventories wait for this handler's verdict: taking up a ground item ('pickup'), dropping ('drop'), eating, drinking or applying an item or a pot's serving ('use'), a shop basket ('vendor'), a basket on another player's shelf ('trade'), taking from or putting into a container ('stashTake', 'stashPut'), taking from a body ('loot') and putting tack on or off a horse ('horseGear'). The handler receives the transaction { id, kind, player, revision, money, lines: [{ item, name, amount, metadata, row, price, from, to }] } with, by kind, groundItem, stash, owner, vendor, seller, horse or pot, and a verdict function. Return true or false, or a promise of either, or call verdict(true) or verdict(false, reason) later. Every handler must allow an action. A player's actions wait in line and commit one after another, against the inventories as they are then. An action not decided in 5 seconds is refused, and so is one whose handler throws. A refused action changes nothing, and the player's game shows what the server holds. Without a handler, actions commit at once. Returns the handler's id.

params.handler: Called with the transaction and the verdict function.

stopBeforeCommit.summary: Removes a beforeCommit handler. A resource's handlers also go when it stops.
stopBeforeCommit.exampleLua:
local Inventory = kcds.players.Inventory

local handlerId = Inventory.beforeCommit(function() return true end)
Inventory.stopBeforeCommit(handlerId)
